nodes.name: PhantomBuster Webhook
nodes.notes: responseMode=onReceived acks PhantomBuster immediately (its webhook timeout is 11s) so downstream processing never risks a timeout retry/duplicate delivery.

nodes.name: Fetch Result JSON
nodes.notes: The webhook's inline body.resultObject was null on this agent even on a successful run — PhantomBuster doesn't embed output for every phantom type. This calls /containers/fetch-result-object with the containerId from the webhook instead, which is the documented way to pull a specific run's result on demand. Set the same 'Header Auth' credential used on the kickoff workflow's Launch node (X-Phantombuster-Key) here too.

nodes.name: Split Out Candidates
nodes.notes: Once you see a real successful run here, check this node's output — if it's empty despite the phantom finding profiles, the raw structure from Fetch Result JSON needs inspecting (click that node's output) and this parsing logic adjusted to match.

nodes.name: Pace (Groq free tier: 30 req/min)
nodes.notes: llama-3.3-70b-versatile free tier caps at 30 requests/minute. One request every 2.5s keeps this comfortably under that regardless of how many candidates are in this batch.

nodes.name: Groq - Qualify Candidate
nodes.notes:
Set the 'Header Auth' credential on this node after import: Name = Authorization, Value = Bearer YOUR_GROQ_KEY (include the word 'Bearer' and a space before the key — Groq needs the full string as the header value). OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint. response_format json_object asks the model to force valid JSON output — supported on llama-3.3-70b-versatile.

Prompt includes companySize/industry fields from the candidate object, but it's unconfirmed whether PhantomBuster's Account Employees Export actually returns these — check a real 'Split Out Candidates' output; if those fields aren't present, the prompt safely falls back to 'Unknown' rather than breaking, but the company-context scoring factor from spec §7 won't have real data to work with until confirmed.
